summary: Steel fire tower on Bald Mountain in Townshend State Forest, erected in the 1930s; dismantled in 1949 and moved to Mount Olga. No tower on the summit today.

facts.status_note: The Bald Mountain tower was taken down in 1949; the steel lookout was moved to Mount Olga in Molly Stark State Park

access.note: Bald Mountain Trail, 1.7 miles, leads to the summit in Townshend State Park. An undated park alert says the trail is temporarily closed after a footbridge washed out.

visit.trail_note: 1.7-mile Bald Mountain Trail from Townshend State Park; temporary closure per undated park alert

events.note: Watchman at a cabin and telephone station on Bald Mountain; state report says no tower was necessary
More forest fires reported from this station than from any other of the state's 14 mountain lookouts
Newspaper reports work complete on a new observation tower; the state park history dates a fire tower to 1924
CCC members of the 119th Company erected a steel fire tower on Bald Mountain, per a state report; a 1949 newspaper gives 1934
Old wooden tower razed, per state report
Nathan Dauchy named to the lookout tower post
Steel tower taken down in August 1949 to be set up on Mount Olga
Steel lookout moved to Mount Olga, per the National Historic Lookout Register; a hiking guide dates the move to 1955

evidence.supports: 1913 watchman, cabin and telephone, no tower
evidence.quote: 1913: A watchman is employed at the lookout station on Bald Mountain in Townshend. This station consists of a cabin and telephone, but no tower was necessary.

evidence.supports: June 1922 arrangements for a new tower; old tower outlived its usefulness
evidence.quote: June 24, 1922: Mr. Delavan remained in the southern part of the state for continued inspection of fire lookout stations. He is to make preliminary arrangements for a new lookout tower at Townshend, the old tower having outlived its usefulness.

evidence.supports: July 1922 work on the new observation tower completed
evidence.quote: July 21, 1922: Work on the new observation tower at the forestry lookout station on Bald mountain was completed some time ago

evidence.supports: state park history dates the fire tower to 1924
evidence.quote: A fire tower was built in 1924 to protect the forest, but it was removed in 1949.

evidence.supports: 1933 plan for a steel tower to replace the old one
evidence.quote: September 23, 1933: In Townshend a road is to be built to the top of Bald mountain where the old state fire lookout tower will be replaced by one of steel.

evidence.supports: 1936 CCC erection of a steel tower in Townshend State Forest
evidence.quote: 1936: Members of the 119th Company CCC of Bellows Falls erected a steel forest fire tower on Bald Mountain, Townshend State Forest.

evidence.supports: 1949 newspaper gives 1934 as the build year
evidence.quote: Built in 1934, the Bald Mountain tower has had only secondary use

evidence.supports: 1921 fire reports exceed other state lookouts
evidence.quote: During the 1921 season more forest fires were reported from this station than from any other of the 14 state mountain lookouts.

evidence.supports: 1924 part-time manning for lack of funds
evidence.quote: The lookout in Townshend is manned only part time, because of a lack of funds.

evidence.supports: August 15, 1924 date of the part-time item
evidence.quote: August 15, 1924

evidence.supports: Nathan Dauchy named to the lookout post in 1938
evidence.quote: October 14, 1938: Nathan Dauchy has been named to the lookout tower post on Bald Mountain in Townshend.

evidence.supports: old wooden tower razed
evidence.quote: June 1938: Constructed new metallic telephone line to tower. Installed lightning protection on lookout tower. Installed telephone instrument in tower. Razed old wooden tower.

evidence.supports: 1949 steel tower being dismantled for Mount Olga; 50-foot height
evidence.quote: August 15, 1949: The 50-foot steel tower on Bald Mountain in Townshend is being dismantled and will be set up next week on Mt. Olga.

evidence.supports: 1949-50 state report: tower taken down to be erected on Mt. Olga
evidence.quote: 1949 - 1950: Steel fire tower taken down, to be erected on Mt. Olga. Telephone line salvaged.

evidence.supports: NHLR: Mount Olga steel lookout moved from Bald Mountain in 1949
evidence.quote: The present steel lookout with 7x7’ metal cab was moved to the site from Bald Mountain in 1949 and was in use until the 1970s.

evidence.supports: Mount Olga tower lies in Molly Stark State Park
evidence.quote: The tower is maintained as a popular hiking destination and view point in Molly Stark State Park.

evidence.supports: hiking guide dates the Olga move to 1955
evidence.quote: This is a steel structure originally built at Townsend State Forest and moved to the Mount Olga summit in 1955.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the Bald Mountain tower as gone
evidence.quote: Bald Mountain Windham 43.03275 -72.68906 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a standing tower at Mount Olga
evidence.quote: Olga, Mount Windham 42.85081 -72.80318 Tower Standing

evidence.supports: Bald Mountain Trail is 1.7 miles to the summit
evidence.quote: The Bald Mountain Trail is a 1.7 mile, moderate trail leading visitors to the summit of the mountain.

evidence.supports: undated closure after footbridge washed out
evidence.quote: Due to flooding, the footbridge on the Bald Mountain trail was washed out. The trail is temporarily closed until the bridge can be repaired.

corrections.why: The town and the state park are spelled Townshend on the park's own page; the Townsend spelling appears only in some older lists

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1922 newspaper reports completed work on a new observation tower; the state park history dates a fire tower to 1924. The story gives both and does not choose.
A 1949 newspaper gives 1934 as the steel tower's build year; a 1936 state report records CCC members erecting it that year. The story gives 1936 as the erection and notes the 1934 claim.
The register and the 1949 state reports tie the move to Mount Olga to 1949; a hiking guide gives 1955. The story uses 1949 and notes the 1955 claim.

sources.title: Mt Olga Fire Tower, Marlboro VT

notes_for_editor: Forest Lookouts gives the richest history, with the 1949 removal confirmed by the state park page and the NHLR. Dates disagree in three places (first tower 1922 vs 1924; steel tower 1934 vs 1936; Olga move 1949 vs 1955), and the story says so. The weebly page spells the town Townsend in places and Townshend in others; the park uses Townshend. The Westmore Bald Mountain (us-vt-bald-mountain, Orleans County) is a different tower. No source describes what remains on the Townshend summit. The trail closure notice is undated and may be out of date. No photos found.
